sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

content.text:
# A box that drops and lands

I want a physics demo: a box starts up in the air, falls under gravity, and lands on a flat floor,
then comes to rest. Make the box a solid blue so it's easy to see, and give it a plain gray floor to
land on.

It should just play on its own when the project runs — no clicking needed.

content.text:
The demo is built: when the page loads, a solid blue box falls from 5 m up, lands on a plain gray floor, tips onto a face and comes to rest. You don't need to click anything, and you can still drag the camera to look around.

**What I checked:**
- **Physics test:** stepping the simulation for 6 seconds, the box falls under gravity and never sinks into the floor. It settles flat on the surface and stops moving completely by the last second. The physics engine also reports it at rest.
- **In the browser:** I took screenshots of the built page with no console errors. At 0.7 s the box is mid-air with its shadow on the floor. At 4.7 s it is resting on the floor.
- **Existing checks:** the project's startup browser tests pass, and so does a new small test of the scene setup.

**Choices you might want to change:**
- The box starts slightly tilted so it tips onto a face when it lands; without the tilt it would land flat. You can change the angle near the box in `src/drop/index.ts`.
- To keep the floor looking truly gray, I changed both lights to plain white. With the original warm lighting it looked beige.
- I removed the original turning-cube welcome scene. Since its test was the project's only one, I added the scene-setup test so `bun test` (which CI runs) still has something to run.

**Files:**
- `src/drop/index.ts`: the demo scene (box, floor, lights, camera).
- `src/drop/drop.test.ts`: checks there's one moving box above one fixed floor (run by `bun test`).
- `tests/drop.node.ts`: the full fall-and-settle check (run with `bun test ./tests/drop.node.ts`).
- `index.html`: now starts the demo and has an updated page description.

Run it with `bun run dev`.
